title: WebView Origin and Capability Security Check

questions.prompt: Which design best applies webview origin and capability security?
options: Prefer external browser surfaces; otherwise allowlist parsed origins and expose only minimal origin-bound native capabilities.
questions.answer: Prefer external browser surfaces; otherwise allowlist parsed origins and expose only minimal origin-bound native capabilities.
questions.explanation: The strongest option enforces authority at the correct boundary and includes limitations, lifecycle, adversarial verification, and recovery.

questions.prompt: An HTTPS top-level page guarantees every iframe and JavaScript message originates from the same trusted host.
questions.explanation: Allowing a URL because its string contains bank.example accepts crafted authorities, paths, user-info, and schemes that do not share the trusted origin.

questions.prompt: Why is a generic JavaScript bridge dangerous?
questions.answer: It can turn untrusted web content into a caller of powerful native capabilities without a reliable least-privilege origin contract.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the specific security property and boundary required by the lesson rather than naming a library.
